text:
maria: Heads-up — ran into a weird case in the multi-region sim: when a region briefly loses connectivity, we can end up with split caches for the same tenant and different active primaries. How do folks think we should reconcile without violating residency guarantees?

ken: do we have reproduction steps? sounds like classic split-brain for cache ownership.

maria: repro: start tenant pinned to eu-west, deploy interruption, traffic shifts to us-east (fallback). both keep writing their local prefix caches. after network heals, we have conflicting prefixes + differing kv versions.

ashley: if the tenant is EU-residency (customer compliance), we can't move their source-of-truth out of eu-west. any reconciliation that copies eu data to us-east is a no-go. we need ownership-preserving resolution.

ken: agreed. options: 1) deterministic owner by tenant hash -> authoritative region. on reconnect, other regions tombstone local cache keys and pull from owner. 2) lease/epoch handoff: owner issues a lease, others check before accepting writes.

sanjay: +1 for lease-based, but we need a safe fast path for brief partitions. what about a "confirm-first" write flow: if a region thinks it's not owner, it writes locally but marks as provisional; reads prefer owner; background reconciliation promotes provisional once owner ACKs or after TTL.

kai: provisional writes sound right but tricky for latency. suggestion: keep provisional local writes but add a tiny metadata header: origin-region + logical-timestamp + residency-flag. On reconcilation pass, owner can NACK or accept. If owner NACKs, we GC the provisional entry and emit a compensating write.

maria: we also need to avoid blowing up token costs with huge re-fetches on reconciliation runs. any ideas for rate-limiting or incremental catch-up?

ken: we can do per-tenant change streams + watermark checkpointing. each region keeps a checkpoint per-tenant of the last reconciled seq. backfill only deltas.

ashley: legal constraint reminder: anything that causes eu-origin data to be forwarded to non-eu for processing is either blocked or needs explicit customer opt-in. so owner-based pulls are fine, push-based synchronization across boundaries is not.

sanjay: then the protocol should be pull-first: non-owner must request the authoritative keys from the owner (no automatic push). owner returns either full value or a tombstone directive. non-owner then applies accordingly.

maria: can we outline a simple handshake?

ken: sketch:
```
# on reconnect: non-owner scans local provisional keys -> for each key K:
# 1) call owner: GET /reconcile?tenant=T&key=K&since=local_ts
# 2) owner returns {status: accept|reject|tombstone, value?, version}
# 3) non-owner: if accept -> promote local provisional to canonical; if reject/tombstone -> delete/local-gc
# owners rate-limit and provide checkpoint window
```

kai: add one more: owner may return a "defer" when it's in a sensitive migration or audit window; non-owner should backoff and schedule retry. include an idempotent reconcile-token so retries don't duplicate work.

ashley: audit logs requirement: every reconcile decision must be logged with reason (accept/reject/defer) and correlation id. we need this for compliance audits.

maria: good call. also need to set TTLs and tombstone grace to avoid resurrecting old keys on late arrivals. maybe tombstone TTL = 7 days? open to pushback.

ken: 7 days seems long but safe. can we make it parameterized by tenant classification? low-risk tenants 24h, high-risk/regulatory 7d.

sanjay: operational note: reconciliation load can spike on region recoveries. put a circuit-breaker and progressive warm-up: 1) background checkpoint resync (low qps), 2) on-demand reconcile for active traffic, 3) full backfill async.

kai: also surface a "reconcile-state" metric per-tenant and per-region: pending_keys, last_reconciled_ts, last_owner_response. that helps SLOs.

maria: testing plan: unit tests for handshake states, chaos tests simulating split brain, and an integration test that asserts no cross-region push for EU tenants. canary roll with 1% tenants.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary-reconcile-protocol v0.1 -> staging at 2245603745 :rocket:

ashley: docs: make compliance section explicit in the API contract (owner-only data transfer). I'll draft language.

ken: next action items: ken -> prototype lease handshake and tombstone TTL config; sanjay -> rate-limit/circuit-breaker design; kai -> metrics + idempotent token design; ashley -> compliance copy for API contract; maria -> chaos test harness.

maria: thanks everyone — I'll put these as follow-ups in a short RFC update and schedule a 30m sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:

ken: +1

sanjay: +1

kai: +1

ashley: +1
